item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commissioner Against Corruption surveyed staff at the state’s three public universities about integrity and workplace experiences.
item.support:
a 
survey designed to better understand the attitudes and experiences of public officers 
employed by the state’s three public universities

item.text: The Commissioner reported concerns among respondents about safe reporting, protection from reprisals and whether universities would act on reports.
item.support:
Only one in four agreed their employer had adequate 
protections in place for those who report corruption or inappropriate conduct.

item.text: The Commissioner concluded that integrity risks and workplace cultures differed across university areas, requiring attention to local circumstances.
item.support:
Consequently, universities may benefit from investigating these local 
cultures and tailoring strategies accordingly.

item.text: The Commissioner urged universities to improve reporting cultures and check whether staff understood and followed existing policies.
item.support:
Universities should review how they can improve the culture of reporting across the 
breadth of their organisations

item.quote:
It is clear that the experiences and attitudes of university public officers can vary 
markedly between different areas of a university.
